author: /root/norm_bridge_audit_49
body: Initial audit: the forward coordinate-to-operator estimate is mathematically sound provided “coordinate expansion” means an exact expansion of each unit vector in the chosen basis with sum of absolute coefficients ≤ d (for orthonormal Euclidean coordinates, equality d); multilinearity then gives ≤ d^n C. More generally the stated assumptions should explicitly include coefficient-sum bound ≤ d, or replace d^n by the product of those bounds. For n=0, Fin 0 tensor is the scalar value, the empty expansion has one term, d^0=1, so the bound is exactly C; handle this case explicitly in induction. Reverse operator-to-coordinate bound has factor 1 when each coordinate vector has norm ≤1. The reverse of the forward claim (coordinate components ≤C imply operator norm ≤C) is false: on Euclidean R², n=1, L(x,y)=x+y has both coordinate values 1 and operator norm √2. For prefixes j≤n, a common coordinate cap C yields per-order operator bound d^j C ≤ d^n C (for d≥1); conversely full-operator cap C gives every coordinate component cap C. Prefix at n=0 is just order 0 and constant factor 1. Quantifiers must be: for each n,d, space/basis satisfying the expansion hypotheses, each continuous n-linear map T, and each C≥0, if every coordinate tuple evaluation has norm ≤C then ‖T‖≤d^n C; no function-specific constant is introduced. Nonnegativity is needed to multiply inequalities safely. This abstract result alone does not identify paper C_y^m: report says no explicit norm convention was located; it supplies finite-dimensional equivalence under a chosen full-Frechet convention, not source evidence that the paper uses coordinate partial maxima or the same scalar/torus convention.
